segments.he: אות י

כי מרדכי הוא דרור. דרור לשון חירות בחינת יובל שהיא שנת החמשים בחינת חמשים שערי בינה. ובינהמקננא בכורסייא שהיא בחינת כסאות למשפט כנ"ל כי אחיזת מרדכי היה במקום גבוה מאד מאד שהוא סוד התגלות חכמה סתימאה שהוא נתגלה בעת השינה והדורמיטא דייקא. כי דייקא בעת השינה היינו כשמסלקין כל החכמות שהוא בחינת שינה אז נתגלה הארת מרדכי שהוא התגלות חכמה סתימאה היינו שנתגלה החכמה הסתומה ונעלמה מעין כל. היינו בחינת השגת צדיק ורע לו רשע וטוב לו שעל ידי זה נתתקן בחינת כסאו למשפט כי זה בחינת תיקו המשפט כנ"ל (ועיין היטב בפרי עץ חיים בכוונת של פורים ובדברי רבינו הנ"ל היטב):והמן הרשע שרצה להתגבר על מרדכי על ידי פגם המשפט היינו פגם כסאות למשפט ח"ו על כן היתה עצתו לעשות עץ גבוה חמשים אמה לתלות את מרדכי עליו. כי רצה לפגום בבחינת חמשים שערי בינה שהם בחינת כסאות למשפט שמפגם זה היהת אחיזתו כנ"ל. וזהו סוד הגורל שהפיל כי שם הוא שורש הגורל היינו כי בבינה שהוא בחינת כסאות למשפט שם הוא סוד הגורל כי משם יוצא המשפט לכל באי עולם ונותנין לכל אחד פי גורלו ומשפטו. וזהו בחנית הגורל של הכהן גדול ביום הכפורים כי יום הכפורים הוא בסוד היובל בחינת חמשים שערי בינה כמובא ואז נתתקנין כסאות למשפט ואז הכהן גדול נכנס לפני ולפנים. ואז הכהן גדול היה מטיל גורל על שני השעירים גורל אחד לד' וגורל אחד לעזאזל כי משם ולמטה מתחיל אחיזת הדין שמשם יניקת הסטרא אחרא בחינת עזאזל וצריכין ביום הכפורים שאז נתתקנין כסאות למשפט לתקן הגורל דקדושה בחינת משפט דקדושה ועיקר תיקונו על ידי שמגרשין משם אחיזת הסטרא אחרא ונותנין לו חלקו דהיינו שעיר אחד לעזאזל. שזה בחינת שאין רוצין להעלות בחינת טיפת עשו וישמעאל שהוא בחינת תוקף הסטרא אחרא זוהמת הנחש אל הקדושה דהיינו אל המוח ח"ו רק אדרבא אנו מוציאין אותה לחוץ כי אנו בעצמינו נותנין לו חלקו. דהיינו שעיר אחד לעזאזל כדי שלא יהיה נאחז אצלינו כדי שלא יהי נפגם המשפט ח"ו על ידי זה. ועל כן המן שהיה נאחז מפגם המשפט מפדם הגורל על ידי שפגם שאול ורצה להעלות טיפת עשו וישמעאל אל המוח כנ"ל ועל כן הפיל פור הוא הגורל כי רצה להפוך הגורל והמשפט על ישראל לרעה ח"ו על ידי שנפגם המשפט והגורל כנ"ל ועל כן עשה עץ חמשים אמה. כי רצה לשלוט במרדכי על יד פגם המשפט שהוא בחינת יובל בחינת חמשים שערי בינה כנ"ל. כי על ידי פגם המשפט ח"ו נתעורר ח"ו עמלק כנ"ל. ואחר כך כשזכו ברחמי ד' לתיקון המשפט על ידי מרדכי כנ"ל נתהפכה מחשבתו הרעה על ראשו ותלו אותו על העץ אשר הכין למרדכי כי נתתקן בחינת כסאות למשפט ומה היה נפגם נתתקן ואז נעקר המן עמלק משורש אחיזתו ונתלה על העץ הגבוה נ' אמה. כי משם בעצמו נעקר ונפל לשאול תחתיות כי נתתקן המשפט ונתגרש ונפרד משם המן עמלק שזה בחינת תליה שמעלין אותו עד ראש העץ שגבוה חמשים אמה ומשם דייקא מורידין ומפילין אותו כדי לעקור אותו מן הקדושה לגמרי היינו מבחינת חמשים שערי בינה המלובשין בכסאות למשפט שמשם רצה לינק על ידי פגם המשפט וכנגד זה עשה עץ גבוה חמשים אמה ועתה שזכו לתיקון המשפט משם בעצמו היתה מפלתו כי נעקר משם והורד לשאול תחתיות שזה בחינת תליה שמעלין אותו עד ראש העץ ומשם מורידין ומפילין אות וכנ"ל. כדי לעקור אותו משורשו כנ"ל. וכן נתהפך הגורל והמשפט לרעה על זרע עמלק הכל על ידי תיקון המשפט שהוא בחינת גורל ואז נעקרו ונמחו הם על ידי אותו הגורל דייקא כי נתתקן הגורל שהוא בחינת תיקון המשפט כנ"ל.
segments.en: Therefore the downfall of the wicked through their teeth is excellently juxtaposed with the greatness of Shabbos. All who stand against Yisrael to devour them — "they hissed and gnashed their teeth" (Eichah 2) — their downfall will be through Shabbos holiness, the Tzadik's holiness, when the rectification is through the thirty-two teeth — the instruments of eating — through which the blood of the heart is refined. All who oppose this — the kelipah of Amalek — their teeth will grow long to their detriment, through Shabbos holiness whose essential holiness is eating through the teeth. For the thirty-two teeth are the aleph of Adam, through which the aspect of Adam is made — as in os 51 regarding Erev Yom Kippur. This is the aspect of Kiddush over wine on Shabbos, derived from (Shemos 20): "Remember the day of Shabbos to sanctify it" — "remember it over wine" (Pesachim 106). The essential Kiddush is to draw Shabbos holiness upon oneself, to sanctify all the sparks and souls refined during the weekdays that ascend at Shabbos's onset. Now we draw holiness upon them through Kiddush. Therefore we say Vayechulu over the cup, beginning "The sixth day, and the heavens were completed…" — the entire passage speaks of how on the seventh day, Shabbos, the work was completed through the cessation and rest drawn upon all creations — "Shabbos came, rest came" — the completion and purpose of all His work. As Rashi explained: "What was the world lacking? Rest…" All this we mention at the start of Kiddush over wine — for the entire Kiddush is to draw Shabbos-rest's holiness upon all weekday labors, which are berurim that ascend on the sixth day toward evening at Shabbos's onset, to be included in their purpose — Shabbos holiness, the purpose of heaven and earth. Therefore we sanctify over wine specifically. Refining the holy sparks from weekday contamination to sanctify them in Shabbos holiness — this is cutting off Amalek's seed through the lower point, the aspect of Yehoshua, subduing the blood of the chalal has'mali. Therefore we sanctify over wine specifically — wine is the strengthening of the blood: "Do not look upon wine when it reddens — its end is blood" (Sanhedrin 70 on Mishlei 23). One must be very careful about wine, especially on weekdays. Yet in holiness there are times when it is a mitzvah to drink wine — this is Kiddush over wine specifically. At Shabbos's onset, the blood of the chalal has'mali is subdued — then the wine is in holiness: "he merited — it gladdens him" — "wine gladdens the heart of man." Through the wine over which we sanctify, holiness is drawn upon all ascending sparks through the rectification of the lower point. For their essential ascent is through simchah (os 45). Amalek — the muddying of the blood — is the aspect of sadness, from which the strengthening of desires whose totality is the desire of mishgal: "that he chanced upon you on the way" (Devarim 25). On weekdays it is hard to subdue him through wine — most do not merit the gladdening wine, and then "he did not merit — it devastates him." But at Shabbos's onset one must draw Shabbos joy through the cup of wine over which one sanctifies — then it is the gladdening wine. Through this, holiness is drawn upon the blood — the souls and sparks ascending — and through the blood of the heart one burns for Hashem in "flames of the fire of Yah" — Shabbos holiness is drawn upon all the sparks, their entire purpose. This is "song is said only over wine" (Berachos 35, Arachin 11) — their essential ascent is through song and praise to Hashem: the ten kinds of melody, "A psalm, a song for the Shabbos day" — the ultimate delight of the World to Come, "a day entirely Shabbos," when they will merit the preserved wine and song will awaken in the world — as in the holy Zohar (Tikkun 10, 24b). The essential ultimate rectification of all weekday labors is through the holiness of the Beis HaMikdash — the upper point — upon all thirty-nine melachos (derived from the Mishkan). The meraglim damaged the Beis HaMikdash by slandering Eretz Yisrael, when its destruction was decreed: "You wept…" (Ta'anis 29). All their damage was through the grapes — the damage of wine, through which Adam HaRishon sinned: "She squeezed grapes and gave him" (Bereishis Rabbah 19). Noach too stumbled upon leaving the teivah. Most spies took the cluster of grapes: "and the days were the days of the first-ripening of grapes" (Bamidbar 13) — all their sin's stumbling was through grapes from which wine is made, through which their minds went astray saying it was impossible to conquer Eretz Yisrael. Their essential error was through the kelipah of Amalek — they had great da'as and saw Amalek was exceedingly powerful, but did not overcome to nullify their understanding before Moshe Rabeinu who had the power to subdue it. They frightened Yisrael through Amalek specifically: "Amalek dwells in the Negev" (Bamidbar Rabbah 16). They stumbled through the grapes specifically — for there the kelipah of Amalek grips more: "their grapes are grapes of poison, bitter clusters" — the strengthening of the blood. Yehoshua was saved from the spies' counsel through Moshe's power — he subdues and cuts off the kelipah of Amalek, so he was not ensnared by their grapes. On the contrary, he merited bringing all Yisrael into Eretz Yisrael. Therefore at Kiddush, when the lower point — Yehoshua — shines, we sanctify over wine specifically, for then the wine is in holiness. Yehoshua cut off the evil blood of the chalal has'mali — then wine is the gladdening wine: "song is said only over wine." Therefore on Purim, the essential cutting off of Amalek's seed, it is a great mitzvah to become intoxicated — Amalek is subdued through wine specifically, meriting simchah, for his essential subduing is through simchah. This is the seventy words of Kiddush — to subdue the seventy nations whose totality is Amalek. The ayin [70] of Amalek is subdued through the wine of holiness in Kiddush, which equals seventy. This is what our Sages expounded: "Remember the day of Shabbos to sanctify it" — "remember it over wine" (Kiddush), and also: "remember it from the first day of the week." These are one and the same: through Kiddush, holiness is drawn upon all weekday deeds and labors. "Remember it from Sunday" — one must remember Shabbos throughout all six weekdays to draw Shabbos holiness upon them, whose essential completion is through Kiddush over wine. Our words are founded upon what Admo"r z"l wrote in the Torah above, os 4: "When a person wants to walk in the ways of teshuvah, he must be expert in halachah and have two expertises — expert in ratzo, expert in shov, as it says: 'Praiseworthy is he who enters and exits.' This is 'If I ascend heaven, there You are' — ayeil, expert in ratzo; 'and if I make my bed in She'ol, behold You' — nafik, expert in shov." See there at the end, the secret of the Kavanos of Elul, where the plain meaning is explained: whoever wants to return must gird his loins and strengthen himself in Hashem's ways always, in whatever passes over him. See our words in many places where we spoke of this in many formulations, with awesome eitzos to strengthen oneself — the essential thing through the power of the true Tzadik. This is the summary of our words in this entire halachah: to strengthen ourselves through meriting to receive Shabbos, through which we always remind ourselves through the true Tzadik's power — the aspect of Shabbos. These depend upon each other: the more one believes in the Tzadik and draws close, the more one merits drawing Shabbos holiness; through keeping Shabbos with simchah, one merits drawing close to the Tzadik — and through this one merits walking in the ways of teshuvah, drawing the expertise to hold oneself in whatever passes, however it may be. The essential means is through Rosh HaShanah, when they gather together — for the ways of teshuvah are drawn through Elul, Rosh HaShanah, and Yom Kippur. All Yisrael's service during these days is to draw these teshuvah pathways so that Yisrael merit teshuvah, through which the redemption from this exceedingly long exile will be brought near. Its end cannot be fathomed — "the end of wonders" — but it is explained in the Gemara and all Midrashim that the essential matter depends on teshuvah. Therefore the true Tzadikim labor only to draw teshuvah pathways into the world, so that even the very far and fallen will be strengthened in teshuvah, through which everything is rectified. For now Hashem asks only a little arousal: "Let them open in teshuvah like the eye of a needle, and I will open great gates." But even this infinitesimal bit is exceedingly hard to begin without the great Tzadikim who draw the teshuvah pathways to strengthen all who wish to return, wherever they may be. All this is hinted in the Zohar Chadash regarding Noach's teivah (Parshas Noach, 24-25, Slavuta edition): Noach did not beseech for his generation. After leaving the teivah and seeing the whole world destroyed, he began weeping. The Holy One Blessed Be He answered: "Foolish shepherd! Now you say this and not before?" See there: the greatness of Moshe Rabeinu who gave his life for Yisrael; how Noach did not beseech because he did not even think he himself would be saved; how much the Holy One Blessed Be He wants people to beseech for Yisrael, even if they are as they are. See what is written on "And he sent the raven" — this is Dovid, who called constantly like a raven; and on "And he sent the dove" until "and she did not return to him again." All of Noach's damage and its rectification is about the expertise above — he was not expert in this halachah of the ways of teshuvah like Moshe and the great Tzadikim who draw teshuvah pathways with wondrous expertise. Noach was a Tzadik tamim, but did not grasp that it was possible to go out, to lower himself, to look upon such wicked people, to engage with them, to find merit in them, to pray for them, to arouse them through some good point — all of which Moshe and the great Tzadikim after him engaged in with tremendous effort. All this is included in the expertise of ayeil and nafik. Therefore Noach thought: "If only I could save myself" — he did not grasp how far His mercies reach. He was forced to enter the teivah — built with lofty wisdom and holiness, with deep kavanos in its dimensions. It hints at teshuvah on Yom Kippur: "Noach's teivah — this is Yom Kippur" (Zohar, Tikkun 21, 54b); "And the teivah rested in the seventh month — this is Tishrei." Also: Noach's teivah is the words of prayers and supplications that Yisrael pray. All of Noach's entering was ayeil — because he could not save himself with the world, not being expert, especially in nafik. Hashem commanded him to enter — ayeil. And just as he needed the command to enter, he needed the command to exit: "Go out from the teivah" — for his leaving was the aspect of nafik. It is written hotzei but read hayatzei; Rashi: "Tell them to leave; if they don't want to, bring them out against their will." They did not want to leave willingly — hinting at everything we have written: whoever wants to return would prefer sitting always in the beis midrash. But Hashem wants the world's continuity — a person must frequently leave for bodily needs and livelihood, all of which is nafik. This is very hard — one knows the danger of going outside — but it cannot be otherwise. Hashem wants one to serve Him in this world specifically — which is entirely nafik relative to the upper worlds — and therefore even here, service must be in ayeil and nafik. This is "and he sent the raven" — the Zohar Chadash explains: Dovid, who called constantly like a raven. Hashem sent him from his kingdom; "And it went out, going and returning" — "Dovid went up the ascent of olives, going and weeping, his head covered" (Shmuel II 15) — he went out and returned in teshuvah, confessing and seeking mercy, until the waters dried. The dove was sent three times, hinting at the exiles until this final one: "she did not return to him again" — this is why this exile is so long. But nevertheless He is prepared and waiting for when she will return. See all this well. Therefore the entire rectification was through the rainbow of the covenant that Hashem promised (Bereishis 9): "My bow I have placed in the cloud." The rainbow of the covenant is the aspect of Rosh HaShanah when the shofar is blown — teki'ah, shevarim, teru'ah — whose sign is kash"t [=keshes, rainbow], as brought in his words z"l. This is the power of the great true Tzadik — the rainbow of the covenant, as in the holy Zohar (Vayikra 15, Pinchas 215). This is Shabbos holiness — the three meals are the three shofar sounds, the three points. He was promised that even within the cloud and very great darkness — "when I bring clouds upon the earth" — even then "the rainbow will be seen in the cloud." Through the Tzadik — the rainbow of the covenant — Shabbos holiness is drawn through the Rosh HaShanah gathering, when the holy sounds — sign kash"t — are blown, sustaining the gathering of Yisrael: "On that day a great shofar will be blown, and the lost in Ashur and the cast-away will come" (Yeshayah 27). Through all this, the teshuvah pathways are drawn — the expertise of ayeil and nafik, to hold oneself even in She'ol Tachtiyos: "and if I make my bed in She'ol, behold You." Through this, Yisrael will fulfill His will — to return at least "like the eye of a needle." As the Zohar Chadash states: "If Kneses Yisrael opens teshuvah like the eye of a needle, I will open great gates." But even this minimal teshuvah is exceedingly hard because the adversary fells one each time — rectifiable only through the expertise drawn by the Tzadik, the rainbow of the covenant. Therefore Hashem promised Noach not to worry upon leaving the teivah — nafik — for Noach saw the great provocation of the yetzer hara. But Hashem promised through the rainbow of the covenant — the true Tzadik encompassing all rectifications, drawing teshuvah pathways — the expertise through which everything is rectified until the complete redemption comes speedily in our days, amen. Therefore we mention in Birchas Zichronos (Mussaf of Rosh HaShanah) at its beginning the matter of Noach: "And also Noach You remembered with love when You brought the Flood waters… therefore his remembrance came before You…" We remind Him of His immense kindness and mercy — how He desires the world's continuity. Even in Noach's days, when such darkness was in the world, He remembered Noach, brought him from the teivah, and promised to sustain the world through the rainbow of the covenant — Rosh HaShanah's holiness. Now that we have already merited the Avos — as we mention their merit afterward: "And I will remember My covenant with Yitzchak" (Vayikra 26) — and Moshe Rabeinu gave us the Torah, and such Tzadikim revealed the holiness of Rosh HaShanah and the greatness of the gathering — now it is fitting that He remember His covenant in their merit and draw upon us the teshuvah pathways, that we merit returning to Him and He to us, until the redemption is brought near speedily (see os 48). This is the aspect of Eiruvei Techumin: where one places the Shabbos meal, from there the Techum Shabbos begins. Shabbos is the aspect of teshuvah, whose essence is the two expertises — expert in ayeil, expert in nafik — the Techum Shabbos of two thousand amos, the two alephim. Through teshuvah an aleph is made. The essential expertise — the teshuvah pathways — is to be extremely careful not to go outside the Techum Shabbos, outside holiness's boundary. The totality of holiness is Shabbos holiness, and this expertise means: in whatever passes over him, one guards oneself not to fall completely, not to go outside the techum. Every person inevitably endures much — especially one who already sinned; when wanting to return, the ocean depths rage — foul thoughts, as understood from the Arizal's writings and our Sages' words. This is essential teshuvah: overcoming so as not to fall completely. It is impossible to detail for each individual — the variations are immense even within one person. But all is included in his holy, awesome words where he called this "expert" — one must be very expert: expert in ratzo and ayeil according to one's level, expert in shov and nafik according to one's level — to fulfill "and if I make my bed in She'ol, behold You": even in She'ol Tachtiyos, never despair. As explained in those conversations and deep eitzos in our books — fortunate is he who grasps them. All this is Techum Shabbos. The essential Shabbos holiness is Shabbos eating — entirely holy — through which teshuvah pathways are drawn. Therefore where one places the Shabbos meal-measure, from there the techum begins — one acquired shvisah there. The essential acquisition of Shabbos rest is through the Shabbos meal. As in siman 277, Likutay I, "Tzadik kaTamar yifrach": the holy path is conquered and broadened through Shabbos eating — "check in the teeth and you will find in the feet" (Shabbos 152). The essential holy path the Tzadik makes — the teshuvah pathways — draws eitzos and hischazekus so that all return to Hashem, even the very weak who desire to return — all will merit through the teshuvah pathways drawn into the world, the aspect of Shabbos, essentially through Shabbos eating. The essential Techum Shabbos is derived from the Machaneh Yisrael, which was twelve mil. Therefore mid'Oraisa the techum is twelve mil. But our Sages enacted only two thousand amos, seeing the great strengthening of the kelipos in exile. These two thousand amos are the measure between the Aron and the Camp: "But there shall be a distance between you and it of about two thousand amos" (Yehoshua 3). Rashi: "Like the measure of Techum Shabbos, so they could go to pray before it." The essential war is the war of Amalek — against the weak ones whom the cloud expelled. Yehoshua fought with Moshe's power so Amalek would not fell them completely: "and he tailed you — all the weakened ones behind you" (Devarim 25). Rather, to return them in teshuvah, bringing them within holiness's boundary — the Machaneh Yisrael, where the Ohel Mo'ed and Aron stood, from which holiness is drawn. The more distant one is, the more holiness and expertise must be drawn from a higher, holier place. Therefore the techum's measure is from the Machaneh Yisrael — the essential techum is that each person remains in the Camp and Amalek cannot cast him out. One constantly strengthens oneself to hold onto the true Tzadikim and their talmidim — Moshe and Yehoshua — who fight Amalek in every generation to return and build the Beis HaMikdash and bring Yisrael back to Eretz Yisrael. This is also Eiruvei Chatzeiros: the essential eiruv rectification is through the Shabbos meal. Through sharing in the Shabbos meal, carrying in and out between domains becomes permitted. Without an eiruv, it is forbidden even between two reshus hayachid domains. The general prohibition of the thirty-nine melachos is the aspect of carrying from domain to domain — berurim (os 30). Our Sages were stringent that even from one domain to another is forbidden — all for the expertise's rectification. Just as one must be careful in ayeil and nafik not to leave one's boundary nor rush beyond it, one must not rush into one's fellow's boundary, in ayeil or nafik. In nafik, certainly chalilah that one look at one's fellow to do as his deeds — one can lose his world in an instant. Dovid HaMelech warned (Tehillim 1): "Happy is the man who has not walked in the counsel of the wicked… nor sat in the company of scoffers." It is known how much the scoffers of the generation bring a person down — especially those calling themselves proper and pious. Hashem should save Yisrael from them. But even in ayeil, one must be very expert not to look at one's fellow who appears righteous compared to oneself, lest one fall — though "envy of scholars increases wisdom" (Bava Basra 21), there is the aspect of "the righteous walk in them and transgressors stumble in them" (Hoshei'a 14). Many fall through jealousy of those who seem more righteous, falling completely in their mind. One must not be a fool but be expert: one's jealousy of better fellows should be for good, to draw closer to Hashem — as hinted in the story of the Chacham and the Tam, where the Tam answered: "That is his work and this is my work." Therefore our Sages enacted that even between domains, carrying on Shabbos is forbidden — so as not to damage the expertise. The rectification is through the Shabbos meal — the eiruv. Through the Shabbos meal the expertise is rectified, then carrying from house to house within the courtyard becomes permitted — the connection between domains will be only for good: they will join in love and peace, each learning from the other for good, drawing closer to Hashem. All this is the expertise in halachah, rectified through the Shabbos meal — the eiruv. This is "And Hashem said to Avram: Lech Lecha — from your land, your birthplace, your father's house, to the land…" and "I will make you a great nation" (Bereishis 12). As explained, the three mitzvos upon entering Eretz Yisrael — cutting off Amalek's seed, appointing a king, building the Beis HaBechirah — are the three points, the aspect of teshuvah. The essential teshuvah is "zarka — cast to the place from where it was taken" — one must leave all the places to which one strayed and return to the source from which one's neshamah was hewn. Every Jew's neshamah-root is exceedingly lofty, but it descended into this world's earthliness for bechirah — so that through this precisely it returns to its source in wondrous completeness. Every person endures many adventures — trials, refinements, ascents and descents without measure — all of Hashem's intention for good: "everything the Merciful One does is for good." All the refinements and trials are the war of Amalek. One must be expert in ayeil and nafik: "and if I make my bed in She'ol, behold You." When one merits enduring — humiliations, bloodshed, refinements, and trials — this is cutting off Amalek's seed, the lower point, through which one merits teshuvah — Keser, the upper point — Moshe, the Beis HaMikdash. The drawing from upper to lower is the vav within the aleph — appointing a king. This is what Hashem said to Avraham — hinting to every person: "Lech lecha" — go to yourself. The essence of a person, what is called "I," is only the neshamah (siman 22, Likutay I). When speaking to a person — "you" or "go" — the intention is the neshamah, the person's essence. The Torah warns: Lech lecha — go to yourself, to your neshamah's source. All your journeying in this world — intend to go to yourself. "Me'artzecha" — from your earthliness, wherever you descended where it seems hard to leave — overcome and go from your earthliness to your neshamah. "Umimoladtecha" — however you were born, whatever physicality, even though this is a great obstacle — "Behold, in iniquity I was formed" (Tehillim 51) — go from your birthplace to yourself. "Umibeis avicha" — family, neighbors, relatives among whom you were raised, from whom there are many obstacles — sometimes physically, sometimes through opinions opposed to truth. From all, go forth to your neshamah. Believe that the Holy One Blessed Be He does not come with tyranny against His creatures — you have the power to stand in all this (Likutay Tinyana, siman 46). "El ha'aretz asher ar'eka" — Eretz Yisrael, the totality of holiness, the Beis HaMikdash, the source of all neshamos. Rashi: "He did not reveal the land immediately, to endear it and reward him for each utterance." This is the essential trial: Hashem does not show a person during the trial what he will merit — if one could see, there would be no trial. Who would throw eternal pleasantness away for momentary foolishness? But the trial is that one does not see — great hischazekus is needed. If one overcomes, one will be rewarded for every utterance beseeched before Hashem — then the good will be exceedingly dear, since one never imagined such pleasantness — as several Tzadikim said (Yerushalmi Avodah Zarah 3:1): "I said: I have labored in vain… yet surely…"

segments.he: אות יא

וזה בחינת מתנות לאביונים שנותנין בפורים. כי צדקה הוא בחינת תיקון המשפט בבחינ משפט חדקה ביעקב אתה עשית וכמבוא בדברי רבינו נ"י במקום אחר במאמר אמור אל הכהנים (סימן ב') שצדקה הוא בחינת משפט בחינת כי אלקים שופט זה ישפיל וזה ירים עיין שם. ועל כן רצה המן לקלקל הצדקה של ישראל ורצה לשקול עשרת אלפים ככר כסף כנגד השקלים של ישראל כמו שאמרו רז"ל כי כל מחשבתו הרעה היתה להגביר ח"ו פגם המשפט כנ"ל. ועל כן כשזכו לנצחו ולהפילו תקנו מתנות לאביונים היינו צדקה שהוא בחינת תיקון המשפט כנ"ל ועל כן צדקה הוא תיקון הברית כמובא. כי תיקוןה משפט הוא תיקון הברית כנ"ל. ואז נשפע השפע אל מלכות דקדושה שזה בחינת שמיני עצרת (כמבואר במאמר הנ"ל) שזהו בעצמו בחינת צדקה שמשפיעין לעני ואביון שוא בחינת נוקבא בחינת מלכות דקדושה דלית לה מגרמא כלום שזהו עיקר תיקון הברית (כמובא במקום אחר).
segments.en: "V'e'escha l'goy gadol va'avarechecha va'agadlah sh'mecha" — the three points. "V'e'escha l'goy gadol" — cutting off Amalek's seed, whose entire war is to cause Hashem's Name to be forgotten and to distance the weak: "and he tailed all the weakened." Whoever subdues him magnifies Hashem's Name by drawing close the distant and weak — "a great nation" through multiplying the holy gathering, the opposite of Amalek's intent. "Va'avarechecha" — drawing blessing from upper to lower point: "like Chermon's dew… for there Hashem commanded blessing" (Tehillim 133) — appointing a king, through whom shefa is drawn (Likutay Tinyana siman 16). "Va'agadlah sh'mecha" — called Avraham with an added hei of da'as — Moshe, the Beis HaMikdash, the upper point. Afterward one still endures ascents and descents — requiring great expertise. Therefore: "Veheyei berachah" — the blessing will endure, one will always remain standing, never falling forever, remaining in the drawing of blessing from upper to lower point. "And Avram went as Hashem spoke, and Lot went with him" — although Avram did as Hashem spoke, Lot — the yetzer hara — went with him always, refusing to separate, for trial and bechirah. Through this precisely, the highest sparks are refined from the kelipos' depths — as Avraham refined from Lot specifically the soul of Mashiach. "And there was famine in the land, and Avram descended to Mitzrayim" — our Sages say this was a great trial: He tells him to ascend to Eretz Yisrael, then causes him to leave. This is all our words: one must be ayeil and nafik, very expert, never falling in mind, never questioning Hashem, only believing "Hashem is righteous and His judgments straight" — all His intention for good. As with Avraham: arriving in Eretz Yisrael, there was famine — forcing him to Mitzrayim, the nafik — yet he withstood the trial until ascending "very laden with cattle, silver, and gold" — sparks refined there. So it passes over every person. As Admo"r z"l writes (siman 8, "Ra'isi Menoras Zahav"): all descents and ascents are hinted in "Avram descended to Mitzrayim" and "Avram ascended from Mitzrayim" — expert in ayeil, expert in nafik. "And he went on his journeys… to the place where his tent had been at first… to the place of the altar he had made there at first, and Avram called there in the Name of Hashem" (Bereishis 13). Rashi: "Also now he called in Hashem's Name." When one overcomes in nafik through all descents until returning to one's place, one must return to the original path — calling in Hashem's Name as at first. He did not fall from his good path through everything that passed — he returns each time to his true path, calling always to Hashem. Also, "there was famine in the land" hints at every person whose going to the marketplace — nafik — is primarily from lacking livelihood. "Avram descended to Mitzrayim" — business preoccupation, the danger of money-lust, the aspect of avodah zarah and Mitzrayim (as in the Ba'al Tefillah story, hinted in Yeshayah 31: "Woe to those descending to Mitzrayim for help"). But the aspect of Avram — the Jewish person expert in ayeil and nafik — even in Mitzrayim, amidst business, overcomes so as not to become stuck, remembering Hashem, refining holy sparks and ascending with them: "And Avram ascended from Mitzrayim."
